newsitem.title: USA: Motorola sees smartcard industry exploding.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees smartcard industry exploding.

text.p: Technology giant Motorola Inc said Thursday it sees the smartcard systems industry which it has just entered as "exploding" in the next five years, growing to a worldwide business of $15 billion.
Earlier, Motorola said it is launching its Smartcards Systems Business as part of its Land Mobile Products Sector.
"We believe the market is exploding -- it could easily expand eight-fold by the year 2001," Merle Gilmore, president of the company's Land Mobile Products Sector, told reporters in a teleconference.
"By that time, it could very well be that there will be more smartcards in the world than telephones," he said.
Motorola cited industry analysts who estimated the worldwide industry would grow to more than $15 billion by the year 2001. In 1996 it was estimated at $3 billion.

Smartcards look like credit cards but have embedded microprocessors that give them the capabilities of a minicomputer. The company said it eventually sees people carrying one or two smartcards and using them to pay the commuter train fare, buy a cup of coffee, do banking, access the office building and so on.

Motorola's semiconductor sector has provided chips for the smartcard industry for some 20 years. The industry has been limited, but Motorola sees it taking off now as the cards become more complex and personalized.
The company said it will provide everything from the actual cards to the readers needed to use them, as well as software and encryption technology.
Motorola would not disclose how much it is investing in the new business, citing company policy, but said it is being funded as a "full business".

"I can only tell you that we're looking at this as a business that has hundreds and hundreds of billions of dollars of potential -- maybe even more -- and it's being funded as a business that has that kind of potential," Gilmore said.
Security analysts said the move is positive, but only time will tell how the market develops, especially in the United States. The largest smartcards market is currently Europe.

"This could be a major, important business for them," said Mona Eraiba, an analyst for Gruntal & Co, adding, however "It is an emerging market...over time we will see if the potential will be realized."

Motorola was quick to point out that it would continue to nurse its relationships with customers who buy chips for smartcards. The company said it is pushing for open architectures and worldwide standards in smartcards.

"We will continue to be a major supplier to the evolving upgrading of microcontroller technology for the smartcard business in all of the segments, and maintain our relationships with our current customers because we keep them separate," Christopher Galvin, Motorola's chief executive, said.
